title: Specs first: features/daw/set.feature, STEPS.md and the cucumber runner with a set checker
description:
## Intent

Write the M1 specs first and watch them fail (outside-in).

## Steps

- `features/daw/set.feature`: the scenarios of the M1 stories (tempo and length; notes as clips; samples travel; chords as locators; mistakes with location), copied from the stories.
- `features/daw/STEPS.md`: the normative step vocabulary (state, Given/When/Then tables), in the style of `features/sources/STEPS.md`.
- `crates/apricity-daw/tests/daw.rs` (`[[test]] name = "daw", harness = false`): cucumber-rs world with a temp dir per scenario; Given steps write `.apr` text, tiny synthetic WAVs (generated with `hound`, a few hundred ms) and matching `*.apricity.json` manifests (beats, warp markers, tuning; see `fixture()` in `crates/apricity-score/tests/compile.rs`); When steps run the export through the library API and, for CLI-only behavior (`--force`, exit codes), through the built `apricity` binary; Then steps gunzip the set and query it with a small XPath-like helper.
- A set checker used after every export: well-formed XML, unique ids, the next-pointee counter above every id, every referenced sample file exists.

## Verification

`CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 safe-run.sh -- cargo test -p apricity-daw --test daw` runs every scenario and each fails for the right reason (missing behavior, not a broken step). Record the failing list in a comment.

## Release

Lands with the first implementation task's commit or as `test(<this task's id>): ...`; no production code here.
